text.insert: This page lists the words that the STE profile allows, replaces, and bans. The full STE approved-word dictionary is the base, and four layers sit on top of it. A later step moves these lists into typed data at
writing/ste/profile.ts
in docs-model. A generator then builds this page from that file.
No lint uses this vocabulary yet. The naming canon follows the proposed defaults in the open decisions on
STE Profile
Vocabulary Layers
Each layer extends or narrows the layer below it. A word that STE approves stays allowed, even if no page in this corpus uses it.
STE Approved Words (Base)
All of the about 900 approved words in the STE dictionary are allowed, each in its approved meaning.
The full list stays local in
proposals/ste-writing-profile-2026-10-02/ste100/
and is never published.
Technical Nouns
Our project nouns extend the base. Each noun has one meaning in this corpus.
Technical Verbs
Software verbs extend the base, including verbs that STE rejects. Each verb has one meaning.
Replacements
Each row swaps a rejected word for a plainer word.
The tier of the row says whether a lint fixes the word or only flags it.
Banned Filler
Filler words add no meaning, so a writer deletes them.
Naming Canon
Use one name for each concept in prose. Code identifiers keep their own names, such as
DocDocument

text.insert: Technical Verbs
These verbs extend the STE base, and each has one meaning. Use each verb only in that meaning.
Software Verbs STE Rejects
STE rejects these verbs, but software pages need them. The profile allows each one as a technical verb, which is a proposed decision.

text.insert: Replacements

Each table maps a rejected word to the word to write. Rows come from public style guides, such as Google, Microsoft, Red Hat, and plainlanguage.gov. A lint must skip code spans, link URLs, quoted words, and these tables, because they mention a word without using it.
Autofix
A lint swaps these words with no review. The swap keeps the inflection, so "utilizes" becomes "uses". After a deletion, it capitalizes the next word.
